1.title: Start here: what do you already know?

q.Task 1a: Task 1a. Write down the names of as many parts of a cell as you can remember. Even one or two is fine.
q.Task 1b: Task 1b. A plant cell and an animal cell are not the same. Write down one difference you already know.
q.Task 1c: Task 1c. Which part of a cell do you think is "in charge"? Why do you think that?

2.title: Meet the cell: the Fact File and two labelling tasks

q.Table: Task 2. Name the numbered parts of the animal cell.
q.Task 4a: Task 4a. Name the three structures that a plant cell has but an animal cell does not.
q.Task 4b: Task 4b. Name five structures found in both plant and animal cells.
q.Task 4c: Task 4c. A student says: "Animal cells have no vacuoles at all." Is this completely correct? Explain in one sentence.

q.Table: Task 5. Match each job to the structure.
Task 6a. Name parts 1–4 of the mitochondrion.
q.Task 6b: Task 6b. The inner membrane is folded into many cristae. Suggest why folds are useful.
q.Task 7b: Task 7b. What is the green substance inside the discs called, and what does it do?
q.Task 8b: Task 8b. Suggest why the nucleus needs holes (pores) in its membrane.
q.Task 9b: Task 9b. Why is it useful for a cell to be able to choose what comes in?

q.Task 10 corrections: Task 10 corrections. Write a corrected sentence for each false statement.
q.Task 11a: Task 11a. A muscle cell contracts all day and needs a lot of energy. Which organelle would you expect to find many of? Explain why.
q.Task 11b: Task 11b. A house plant is not watered for a week and its leaves go floppy. Which structure has lost water, and why does this make the plant floppy?
q.Task 11c: Task 11c. A cell is making a large amount of a protein. Name the two structures involved and say what each one does.
q.Task 11d: Task 11d. Root cells have no chloroplasts. Suggest why. Do root cells still have mitochondria? Explain.

q.Task 13: Task 13. Show what you know, your choice: A draw a labelled plant cell with a sentence per label; B "A day in the life of a glucose molecule"; C a table of all eight structures; D a "cell city". Write which option you chose and paste or summarise your work here.
q.Extra challenge: Extra challenge. A plant leaf cell has chloroplasts AND mitochondria. Explain why a plant needs both, even though the chloroplast already makes food.
q.Predictions revisited: Look back at Task 1. Add everything you have learned since, and correct anything that was wrong.
q.Revision plan: Anything not ticked is your revision list. Which will you revise first, and how?
